assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The model's nineteen selectors: A_CHILD_SIBLING_PLAY, A_MS_RESULTS, A_MS_HATTORI, A_MS_SENIORS, A_MS_TEAM_AND_GAME (the V06.5 and V08.5 middle-school and childhood material at story-local positions), A01_RECIPROCAL_COACH, A02_ELECTION, A03_ROMANTIC_REFUSAL, A03_HYBRID_NEGOTIATION, A04_06_TAMA_AND_REVENGE, A65_SHOPPING (early second term, not after V06), A08_GATHERING, A09_PAUSED_TEACHING, A10_DISCLOSURE_BIRTHDAY, A11_RUPTURE, A11_WITHDRAWAL, A11_TELLING_AND_SET, A12_PRIVATE_READING and A12_LATER_AND_PUBLIC. The V11 state is historical and V12 is an overlay on it; the V10/V11 school-year conflict over Nagisa stays unresolved; the V06 individual win, V08 mirror-match loss, V11 3-2 set and unnarrated V12 exhibition stay distinct; nothing after V12 is established and no earlier state acquires later knowledge.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph's central account (section 2) is that Hinami tries to secure her own correctness through demonstrable performance rather than another person's interpretation, while her practiced roles create real capacities, attachments and pleasures that exceed that proof project. Section 5 separates immediate aims, recurring standards and the deepest interpreted level, and distinguishes cause, reason, meaning and result; section 11 tests eight rival readings with explicit dispositions, and section 13 runs four retrospective tests, one of which (loss-intolerance) fails and forces a stakes-sensitive revision. The model states twelve conditional mechanisms (AM1-AM12), and the effort ledger traces her regime through middle school (section 31.1), the basketball defeat and NO NAME (section 53), the reproducibility test (section 60), causal unknowability (section 67) and retained capacity without a governing reason (sections 71-74). A is not supported: the deepest level is labelled analyst synthesis, the Nagisa formation account is explicitly not exhaustive, Nagisa's intent stays unknown, and the model claims no blind accuracy. The layered, countercase-tested account exceeds a specialist interpretation, so C is not supported.

Section 3 orders developmental bands on two clocks (when it happened and when the reader can know it) from childhood through V11; section 10.1 preserves a six-variable V11 state (competence, confidence, status, self-concept, agency, value ownership), and section 16.9 overlays a V12 tuple that keeps the V11 state historical. The model binds behavior to nineteen phase selectors, each with a stated ceiling, and the effort ledger gives dated regime tables (sections 3.3, 10.1, 29, 31.1, 53, 60, 67, 71, 82). A is not supported: the monograph's V02, V04, V05, V07 and V08 propositions rest on inherited readings rather than fresh primary returns (section 14.5), the V12 self-liking is explicitly possibly temporary, and nothing after V12 exists. Dated, selector-bound states with historical retention exceed C.

The discovery row claims speech. Section 6 treats her speech as situated samples: the self-reported habit おにただ with its origin in a childhood game (V01, HA-P02 P164) and its changing license with Fumiya, the written V06 boast 私の勝ち, the V09 寂しくても平気 kept distinct from 'not lonely', the V11 crisis self-descriptions 私は、空っぽ and 私は、弱キャラだから, the shift to 'nanashi' at demanding moments, public versus tutor registers, and the V10 softer recollection register. The model selects register by task and recipient and states that no freeform Japanese, complete idiolect, pitch or timing is validated. B is not supported because the samples are explicitly not a frequency-complete idiolect and the voice ledger is not curated on this subject. A self-reported habit with located exact wording and recipient distinctions exceeds a prose description, so D is not supported.

Section 7 classifies ordinary evidence by strength: cheese-filled hamburger steak named by two family speakers (V08.5), cheesecake as event-specific comfort in V11 and as part of the V12 birthday she describes as made of things she loves, Buin enthusiasm for craft and world, the V06.5 clothing lesson with affordable practice, Excel and Word goal records in middle school, and the three Found mugs with a stated gift purpose; section 7.8 tabulates each with its limit and rejects the V11 aroma stone as a preference. Probe 12.12 gives a deliberately modest meal expectation and section 16.8 adds V12 sensory memories. B is not supported because the profile rests mostly on single scenes and section 7.8 states that music, reading, fragrance, brand, travel and household preferences are not established. A located, strength-classified profile with explicit limits exceeds D.

Section 8 differentiates Fumiya (reciprocity without symmetrical authority, domain-specific trust), Tama (admired correctness, the wish that she not adapt, and retaliation in her name she did not want), Mizusawa (the V03 refusal as the controlling fact), Mimimi (competitive consequence without designed insecurity), Yuzu and the peer group, Haruka (warmth and the burden of being her reason), Nagisa and Yoko (love not cancelled by explanatory conflict) and Kikuchi (an interpreter, not an authorized inner voice). Section 16.7 gives a V12 recipient table with each boundary, the model's recipient and private-reader controls restrict knowledge transfer, and effort ledger section 73 locates Haruka's received value. A is not supported: the relationship ledger and dyad specialists are not curated, the monograph calls the Kikuchi relation partly indirect and mediated, and the Tama revenge is never mutually processed. Recipient-specific conduct with knowledge routes exceeds C.

Her private focalization is located: the V06.5 middle-school units (rank management, Hattori, the seniors, the inward discussion of emotion at HA-P08 P227-229), the V08.5 units (team defeat, Haruka's game invitation, nanashi and the choice of NO NAME), the V11 mixed-person family retrospective moving into first-person interiority (HA-P20 P1092), and the V12 first-person chapter (p0022), which gives the room and scroll trigger, self-disqualification, guilt, the differentiated memories and the imagined address to Nagisa. The monograph treats her account as privileged but fallible and separates reader access from what Fumiya hears. A is not supported because in V01-V10 she is mostly seen through Fumiya's interpreting narration (the monograph calls her V09 inner response less accessible than her words), the V11 retrospective is not a transcript, and no validation of inner-state prediction exists. Located private access across formation, crisis and V12 exceeds C.

Located conflict across phases: the middle-school concession to three seniors at real cost (V06.5), the V03 end-authority dispute with Fumiya ending in a restated hybrid and a retained proof demand, the V05 engineered punishment of Konno and its continuation past cessation, the V06 admission that the last blow was revenge (effort ledger section 29), the V09 acceptance of Fumiya's proposed pause, the V11 objection to the birthday video that tracks who made it, the objection to Fumiya's secret route through Haruka, and the 3-2 Boxman set she initiates. Section 4.4 states which proposition she concedes and which jurisdiction she protects, and probes 12.4, 12.9 and 12.11 give conditional patterns with stated support. A is not supported: V04 and V05 primary bytes were not freshly read, lead-case agency is uncertain, and no general stopping rule for retaliation is shown. Repeated, differentiated conflict with stated concessions exceeds C.

Some of her own moral reasoning is rendered: recognizing she lacks the right to stop Tama's chosen change (V05), owning the excess against Konno as revenge while maintaining that some things are intolerable to her (V06), justifying the tolerated first quarrel as a training design (V09), and insisting in V11 that good intentions cannot settle whether she must accept a story about her life. B is not supported because much of section 9 is the analyst's ethical reconstruction rather than her deliberation, her reasoning about Konno stops at admission without apology or restitution, her V09 justification is instrumental, and the model treats novel crisis choices as beyond firm constraint. Located first-person reasons in several phases exceed D.

Sections 6.3, 6.5 and 7.4 locate shared game-analogy humor with Fumiya (jointly finishing inferences in the shopping lesson), sarcasm and exaggerated disappointment with a humiliating edge, the playful middle-school boast chosen over false modesty, the childhood demon-king persona and rematch demands with her sisters, mutual teasing with Hattori, and the V12 irritated banter on her return. The monograph distinguishes affectionate, competitive, pedagogical and cruel teasing. B is not supported because the samples concentrate in a few scenes (V01, the V06.5 shopping lesson, V08.5 sibling play) and no repertoire is separated as systematically as her competitive and instructional conduct. Located functions with recipient distinctions exceed D.

Three reviewed items: a mature monograph with independent review through V12, a root-accepted derived-use model, and the effort ledger, whose curated coverage on the discovery row is V01-V02 specialist analysis although its Hinami sections continue through V12. B is not supported because the monograph's fresh primary returns are selective windows in V01, V03, V06, V06.5, V08.5, V09, V10, V11 and V12, while V02, V04, V05, V07 and V08 propositions rest on inherited readings and audit routes (section 14.5); the claim index, character-state, relationship and voice ledgers, integration reviews and the model's evidence and review packet are not curated; and there is no blind accuracy. Mature reviewed coverage of the whole V01-V12 corpus exceeds D.

Affirmative limits and failures are systematic: the V05 harm continued past cessation and admitted as revenge without apology, the V09 quarrel tolerated as practice without the couple's agreement, the concession under senior pressure, the V06 5-1 set loss and V08 3-1 mirror-match loss, the V08 prestige route that names no affirmative end (effort ledger section 46), the V11 withdrawal and failed council handoff borne by others, the refusal of Mizusawa, and the stated tolerance of loneliness rather than its absence. Section 11 rejects eight total readings, section 13.1 shows the loss-intolerance model failing, and section 16.10 rejects ten V12 overreadings. A is not supported because the counterevidence is retrospective, not held out. Systematic affirmative limits exceed C.

Section 3.1 separates event time from disclosure time; the V06.5 shopping lesson is placed early in the second term rather than after V06, V08.5 is treated as mixed chronology with a Christmas frame between V07 and V08, and the V10/V11 school-year conflict over Nagisa is retained unresolved. The V06 individual win inside a 5-1 set, the V08 3-1 mirror loss, the V11 3-2 set and the unnarrated V12 exhibition stay distinct (effort ledger section 78.4); the V11 state is preserved as historical under the V12 overlay, and the model's nineteen selectors each carry a ceiling. A is not supported because the school-year conflict cannot be resolved, the interval between the V12 reading and the career event is unshown, and nothing after V12 exists. Phase-exact routing exceeds C.

scenario_readiness.note: The evidence attests local Japanese wording, one self-reported habitual expression and recipient-conditioned registers, but the model states that no freeform Japanese dialogue, complete idiolect, pitch, timbre, heard timing or acoustic performance is generated or validated, that おにただ cannot become a universal catchphrase distribution, and that a new line cannot be certified by copying a particle. CONDITIONAL is rejected because no condition makes generated quoted speech source-supported; the monograph's section 6.1 says the evidence is a set of situated samples, not a voice generator.

conditions: One named phase selector from A_CHILD_SIBLING_PLAY to A12_LATER_AND_PUBLIC with that phase's actor-known information; capacities from different phases are not combined, and the V11 withdrawal state is not silently reused after V12.

Only the model's admitted domain: familiar teaching of a willing learner, competition and shared play, supported public-recipient calibration, particular attachment and refusal, and tightly bounded withdrawal or post-reading interpretation.

Output is a labelled hypothetical range with competing reasons and costs, never canonical truth; it abstains on Nagisa's cause or intent, Yoko's practice, a clinical label, permanent coping, terminal romance, vocation, the exhibition result and absent people's replies.
Behavior is described in prose; no quoted Japanese speech is generated as canonical.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A single phase from childhood sibling play to the V12 later and public state within the Japanese V01-V12 main volumes, with V06.5 and V08.5 at their story-local positions; later knowledge is not available to an earlier phase and nothing after V12 is established.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Attested recipients in their phase-specific standing: Fumiya as coached student, elite rival and particular other; Tama as admired, protected peer; Mizusawa as a refused suitor and peer; Mimimi as classmate and comparison target; Haruka as younger sister and admirer; Nagisa and Yoko in memory; Kikuchi as author; Hattori and the middle-school seniors and teammates in their bands. An unfamiliar recipient requires supplied standing or the answer abstains.
setting_constraints: School, peer outing, shopping, home, online and offline Atafami play and the V12 school event settings of the Japanese light novels
No student-council office procedure, career, contract or settled vocation beyond what is shown
Private-reader knowledge from the V08.5, V11 and V12 interiors is not transferred to other characters without a shown route
New severe stress, an unseen crisis or a new harm field ends in abstention on the affected outcome

scenario_readiness.note: The model requires phase, recipient and standing, task and audience, knowledge layers, actual request, alternatives and costs, and any permission or refusal as inputs, gives a fixed decision order, and lists failure modes (transferring private-reader knowledge, erasing a known refusal, making performance fake or omniscient, curing through one reception). The monograph's section 12 gives twelve state-conditioned probes with stated support levels, and section 16.9 forbids reusing the early coach or V11 subject for a V12 situation. READY is rejected because no blind or held-out validation is curated, the model calls its producer and independent cases neither independent acceptance of new outputs nor a global grade, and the monograph supplies no calibrated frequencies.

conditions: Only familiar company and low-stakes play, games, shopping, teaching or meals as near analogs of the located scenes, with the recipient's standing and phase supplied.

Located preferences keep their stated scope (cheese-filled hamburger steak is a liked dish, not a favorite or a universal cheese preference; cheesecake is event-specific); no invented music, reading, fragrance, brand, schedule or household routine.
During the V11 withdrawal phase an ordinary invitation is not assumed to be accepted; behavior is described in prose and no quoted speech is generated as canonical.
scenario_readiness.note: Sections 7.1-7.8 classify ordinary evidence with its limits, the model says that under an ordinary in-domain invitation supported play or exchange should remain available, and probes 12.2 (unfamiliar game with Haruka, moderate to strong), 12.7 (thanks for an ordinary kindness, moderate) and 12.12 (family meal) give state-conditioned expectations. READY is rejected because the preference profile rests mostly on single scenes, probe 12.13 gives limited confidence for re-entry during withdrawal, and section 7.8 lists unestablished tastes.

conditions: Only the located mechanisms: objection to others deciding the meaning of her history or circulating it without permission, the risk that anger extends a protective response past cessation when a valued person is humiliated, and the difference between a learner's assent and her own design authority.
A pre-V11, V11 or V12 phase and the recipient's standing are supplied; the output is a range of reasons and responses with their stated support, not a predicted verdict, apology or act.
No forecast of accountability, restitution, forgiveness or a general stopping rule for retaliation; behavior is described in prose and no quoted speech is generated as canonical.
scenario_readiness.note: Her own reasons are located in V05, V06, V09 and V11, and the monograph gives three ethically loaded probes: 12.8 (an adult calls a loss 'for the best', strong for the mechanism, not for one display), 12.9 (a valued person is humiliated, moderate to strong for the risk, not for repetition) and 12.11 (friends share her history 'to help', moderate to strong for a challenge to standing); the model's AM4 and AM7 bound teaching and disclosure. READY is rejected because the dimension grade is C, much of section 9 is analyst judgment, and the model places novel crisis choices beyond firm constraint. NOT_READY is rejected because these probes specify the conditions under which a bounded range is supported; the grade most worth testing is this CONDITIONAL against Mimimi's NOT_READY.

Romantic material is in evidence: the middle-school Hattori relationship with real pleasure, address shifts and an ending without one decisive incident (V06.5), the V03 refusal of Mizusawa through thanks and apology, and no renewed real reply through V12 (his V12 fictional counterpart's challenge is authored speech). Probe 12.10 gives strong support only for the availability of a refusal and low support for accepting or rejecting a new person, and the model's AM5 bars a terminal romantic verdict or a hidden reason; the monograph does not establish reciprocal romance with Fumiya. Retrieving the V03 refusal is supported, but a romance scenario is not; CONDITIONAL is rejected because no in-evidence relationship supplies a positive romantic state to condition on beyond middle school.

conditions: Only coaching a willing learner on a bounded social or presentation task, leading a team or public occasion in a located band, and skilled competitive play, with the learner's own end, the audience and the phase supplied.
Student-council office, a career, the V08 university and firm route and any contract are not modelled; the V11 failed handoff and the labor others took up are preserved.
Behavior is described in prose; no quoted speech is generated as canonical.
scenario_readiness.note: The model's AM1, AM3 and AM4 cover practiced public calibration, results and recipient-dependent teaching; the monograph's sections 3.7 (basketball leadership), 3.10 and 3.15 (coaching and the shopping lesson) and probe 12.3 (a willing novice, stronger for the instructional pattern than for willingness to help every stranger) locate the conduct. READY is rejected because the coaching evidence is concentrated in one relationship, probe 12.4 is moderate outside it, her council work appears mainly through its interruption, and the V08 career route is desire-poor.

known_limits.statement: In V05 she continued harming Konno after the harm to Tama had stopped, and in V06 she owns this as revenge; the admission is not apology, restitution or a general stopping rule for retaliation, and Tama did not want that protection.

Mizusawa's V03 confession received her refusal; later lightness, ordinary contact, his own account and his V12 fictional counterpart do not convert it into reciprocity, and no renewed real reply is shown through V12.
She let the first Fumiya-Kikuchi quarrel happen as practice without their agreement; the V09 suspension of regular meetings was Fumiya's proposal, which she accepted, not a penalty she imposed.

Her V06 individual win came inside a 5-1 set Fumiya won, the V08 mirror match was a 3-1 loss, the V11 first-to-three set was her 3-2 win, and the V12 exhibition and its result are unnarrated; none establishes timeless superiority.

In V12 she admits liking herself a little, Fumiya allows that this may be temporary, and she attends one school event in uniform; this is not shown regular attendance, restored council office, resumed coaching, romance or permanent recovery.

The V08.5 private units, the V11 mixed-person family retrospective and the V12 first-person chapter give the reader access that Fumiya and her peers do not automatically have; only shown communication routes transfer particular content.

Through V12 she still cannot know whether Nagisa's road entry was accident, intention, dizziness or despair; the V10/V11 school-year conflict stays unresolved, and Yoko's practice is not identified as a named religion.
Kikuchi's Alcia, the V12 story's reunion and its speech are fiction-mediated; they are not Hinami's statements of intent or Nagisa's actual last thoughts.
Her V08 route through the University of Tokyo to a highly selective firm is precise but names no affirmatively wanted activity; it is not a settled vocation.
The monograph's V02, V04, V05, V07 and V08 propositions rest on inherited readings and audit routes rather than fresh primary returns, and the V12 returns are selective windows.

The claim index, character-state, relationship, social and voice ledgers, the integration reviews and the model's evidence and review packet are not curated on this subject, and no blind or held-out accuracy is recorded.
No idiolect, frequency distribution, acoustic performance or validated freeform Japanese exists for her.
The curated items give little direct account of how she conducts student-council office; it appears mainly through its interruption in V11.
Music, reading, fragrance, brand, travel, sleep and household preferences are not established.
Whether her self-liking lasts, her future end, family repair, romance and any later outcome are not established; nothing after V12 is assessed.

dimensions.note: The monograph's central account (section 2) is that Hinami tries to secure her own correctness through demonstrable performance rather than another person's interpretation, while her practiced roles create real capacities, attachments and pleasures that exceed that proof project. The evidence says what changes her response: what a result is asked to prove (13.1 rejects uniform loss-intolerance and conditions the response on the stake; 12.2 versus 12.5-12.6), the learner's own end and assent (AM4; 12.3-12.4), whether a valued person is humiliated and whether that person refuses the protection (12.9), whether someone claims authority to narrate her suffering as justified (12.8) or to circulate her history without permission (12.11; AM7), and, in V12, whether the judging frame is revisable (16.4, 16.9; ledger 81.1). Section 4.4 specifies which proposition she concedes and which jurisdiction she protects, and the model's AM1-AM12 state the mechanisms with their ceilings. It predicts her overreach: anger that extends protection past cessation (V05-V06; 5.6), a learner's distress treated as a training design (V09; 9.3), method authority taken as permission (5.5), and withdrawal whose costs others carry (9.5). Not A: the deepest layer is labelled analyst synthesis (5.1), AM2 declines any invariant priority between pleasure and proof, and the model places hidden priorities and novel crisis choices outside firm constraint. Not C: within the located regimes the account discriminates which consideration decides, which exceeds specialist interpretation.

Section 3 orders developmental bands on two clocks (when it happened and when the reader can know it) from childhood through V11; section 10.1 preserves a six-variable V11 state, and section 16.9 overlays a V12 tuple that keeps the V11 state historical. Not A: the monograph's V02, V04, V05, V07 and V08 propositions rest on inherited readings (14.5), the V12 self-liking is explicitly possibly temporary (16.6), and nothing after V12 exists. Not C: dated, selector-bound states with historical retention and an explicit V12 overlay exceed a period profile.

Bounded to register and speech-act function, not lexical idiolect. Section 6 gives a recipient- and purpose-conditioned account: public speech shaped around the social function of an answer, including a joking boast safer than false modesty (6.2); tutor speech organized by questions, verdicts, definitions and small tests, with specific rather than soothing praise and 'nanashi' when a competence standard is invoked (6.3); a shared game-analogy comic register and an abrasive edge (6.3); refusal performed through thanks and repeated apology (6.6); and crisis self-descriptions in the first person (6.7). Located forms anchor it: the self-reported habit おにただ with its childhood origin and changing license with Fumiya (6.4), the written V06 私の勝ち (6.5), 寂しくても平気 kept distinct from 'not lonely', 私は、空っぽ and 私は、弱キャラだから (6.7), and the V12 P267 self-report about no longer clinging to correctness (16.6). Not A: the samples are explicitly not a frequency-complete idiolect (6.1), the model validates no freeform Japanese, and the voice ledger is not curated on this subject. Not C: the evidence states which register serves which act with which recipient, which is a discriminating account at the level of function. Flagged as an overgrading test.

For play there is a discriminating question, what a game is doing in this encounter (7.3), and probes 12.2 and 12.12 give state-conditioned expectations. Not B: outside play the ordinary profile rests mostly on single scenes and gives no account of how she chooses among ordinary options; music, reading, fragrance, brand, travel and household preferences are not established (7.8). Not D: a located, strength-classified profile with a stated rule for play exceeds distributed mentions.

Section 8 differentiates Fumiya (reciprocity without symmetrical authority, domain-specific trust), Tama (admired correctness, the wish that she not adapt, retaliation in her name that Tama did not want), Mizusawa (the V03 refusal as the controlling fact), Mimimi (competitive consequence without designed insecurity), Yuzu and the peer group, Haruka (warmth and the burden of being her reason), Nagisa and Yoko (love not cancelled by explanatory conflict) and Kikuchi (an interpreter, not an authorized inner voice). Section 16.7 gives a V12 recipient table with each boundary; the model's recipient and private-reader controls restrict knowledge transfer; and the ledger's V12 matrix (section 82) separates Haruka, Yuzu, Nakamura and Takei as relay and delivery actors whose motives Hinami only conjectures. Not A: the relationship ledger and dyad specialists are not curated, the Kikuchi relation is called partly indirect and mediated (8.8), and the Tama revenge is never mutually processed (8.2). Not C: recipient-specific conduct with explicit knowledge routes exceeds a relational sketch.

Her private focalization is located: the V06.5 middle-school units, the V08.5 units (team defeat, Haruka's game invitation, nanashi and the choice of NO NAME), the V11 mixed-person family retrospective moving into first-person interiority, and the V12 first-person chapter (p0022), which gives the room-and-scroll trigger, self-disqualification, guilt, the differentiated memories and the imagined address to Nagisa (16.2-16.5; ledger 81.1). The monograph treats her account as privileged but fallible and separates reader access from what Fumiya hears (1, 16.1). Not A: in V01-V10 she is mostly seen through Fumiya's interpreting narration, the V11 retrospective is not a transcript, and her V12 self-interpretation is her present account rather than the recovered truth of every motive (16.9). Not C: located private access across formation, crisis and V12 exceeds inference from behavior.

Located conflict across phases: the middle-school concession to three seniors at real cost (V06.5), the V03 end-authority dispute ending in a restated hybrid with a retained proof demand, the V05 engineered punishment of Konno continued past cessation, the V06 admission that the last blow was revenge, the V09 acceptance of Fumiya's proposed pause, the V11 objection to the birthday video that tracks who made it, the objection to Fumiya's secret route through Haruka, the 3-2 Boxman set she initiates, and the V12 refusal of the delivery followed by resistance during reading (16.3). Section 4.4 states which proposition she concedes and which jurisdiction she protects, and lists the defensive moves that narrow or end the field with stake-dependent meanings, and probes 12.4, 12.9 and 12.11 give conditional patterns with stated support. Not A: V04 and V05 were not freshly read, and no general stopping rule for retaliation is shown. Not C: repeated, differentiated conflict with stated concessions and protected jurisdictions exceeds incidents alone.

Some of her own moral reasoning is rendered: recognizing that she lacks the right to stop Tama's chosen change (V05), owning the excess against Konno as revenge while maintaining that some things are intolerable to her (V06), justifying the tolerated first quarrel as a training design (V09), insisting in V11 that good intentions cannot settle whether she must accept a story about her life, and in V12 noticing that the new story resembles her mother's device while continuing to read (16.3). Not B: these are stable jurisdiction claims and post hoc admissions rather than located weighing of competing considerations; the monograph itself leaves open whether care changes what she permits herself to do (11.3), much of section 9 is the analyst's ethical reconstruction, her reasoning about Konno stops at admission without apology or restitution, and her V09 justification is instrumental. This is a property of the evidence, not a second count of the scope limit. Not D: located first-person reasons in several phases exceed recorded positions.

Sections 6.3, 6.5 and 7.4 locate shared game-analogy humor with Fumiya (jointly finishing inferences in the shopping lesson), sarcasm and exaggerated disappointment with a humiliating edge, the playful middle-school boast chosen over false modesty, the childhood demon-king persona and rematch demands with her sisters, mutual teasing with Hattori, and the V12 irritated banter on her return (16.6, 16.8). The monograph distinguishes affectionate, competitive, pedagogical and cruel teasing. Not B: the samples concentrate in a few scenes (V01, the V06.5 shopping lesson, V08.5 sibling play) and no repertoire is separated as systematically as her competitive and instructional conduct. Not D: located functions with recipient distinctions exceed scattered mentions.

Three reviewed items: a mature monograph with independent review through V12, a root-accepted derived-use model, and the effort ledger, whose curated coverage now runs through V12 with a dated Hinami regime and a V12 crosswalk (sections 79-84). Not B: the monograph's fresh primary returns are selective windows in V01, V03, V06, V06.5, V08.5, V09, V10, V11 and V12, while V02, V04, V05, V07 and V08 propositions rest on inherited readings and audit routes (14.5); the V12 returns are selective (16.11); and the claim index, character-state, relationship and voice ledgers, integration reviews and the model's evidence packet are not curated on this subject. Not D: mature reviewed coverage of the whole V01-V12 corpus plus a dedicated model exceeds distributed evidence.

Affirmative limits and failures are systematic: the V05 harm continued past cessation and admitted as revenge without apology, the V09 quarrel tolerated as practice without the couple's agreement, the concession under senior pressure, the V06 5-1 set loss and V08 3-1 mirror-match loss, the V08 prestige route that names no affirmative end (13.2), the V11 withdrawal and failed council handoff borne by others, the refusal of Mizusawa, and the stated tolerance of loneliness rather than its absence. Section 11 rejects eight total readings, section 13.1 shows the loss-intolerance model failing, section 16.10 rejects ten V12 overreadings, and ledger section 84 lists what V12 leaves unresolved. Not A: the counterevidence is retrospective and the tests are not held out. Not C: systematic affirmative limits exceed gap statements.

Section 3.1 separates event time from disclosure time; the V06.5 shopping lesson is placed early in the second term rather than after V06, V08.5 is treated as mixed chronology with a Christmas frame between V07 and V08, and the V10/V11 school-year conflict over Nagisa is retained unresolved. The V06 individual win inside a 5-1 set, the V08 3-1 mirror loss, the V11 3-2 set and the unnarrated V12 exhibition stay distinct (ledger 78.4, 81.3); the V11 state is preserved as historical under the V12 overlay; and the model's nineteen selectors each carry a ceiling. Section 16.11 records that the V12 questions she recalls match questions already spoken in the V10 ride, which separates earlier heard content from new private reflection. Not A: the school-year conflict cannot be resolved, the interval between the V12 reading and the career event is unshown, and nothing after V12 exists. Not C: phase-exact routing with located in-volume changes exceeds a loose period.

conditions: Use is illustrative reconstruction of a named selector, labeled noncanonical, never attributed quotation; any line presented as canon is one of the located forms.
No freeform Japanese is generated: illustrative speech is rendered as a paraphrase or translation at the level of speech act, and おにただ or another local word is not distributed as a catchphrase.

The speech act follows recipient, task and phase: function-shaped public answers, question-and-verdict instruction with Fumiya, reciprocal game challenge, refusal through thanks and apology, and direct first-person crisis statements only in the located crisis states; private inner address is never voiced as speech to another person.

Content is fixed by the selector's knowledge route; reader-only interior (V08.5, the V11 retrospective, V12 p0022) is not spoken to people who have not received it, and Nagisa's cause or intent is never supplied.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence constrains generated speech enough for illustrative use at the level of speech act and register: the section 6 recipient and purpose account, the located forms (おにただ with its license, 私の勝ち, 寂しくても平気, the V11 crisis self-descriptions, the P267 self-report) and the model's seven act types. Not knowing her exact wording is productive uncertainty. The model states that no freeform Japanese, complete idiolect, pitch or timing is generated or validated, so Japanese surface generation stays excluded and おにただ is not distributed as a catchphrase. Not READY: there is no idiolect, frequency or lexical model, and the voice ledger is not curated. Not NOT_READY: the predecessor's NOT_READY treated the model's use bound and section 6.1's 'situated samples, not a voice generator' as a finding that all generation is unsupported; under the owner rulings these bound use.

conditions: One named selector, split at located changes inside a volume, with that phase's actor-known information; capacities from different phases are not combined, the V11 withdrawal state is not silently reused after V12, and later developments are never moved earlier.

Only the model's admitted domain: familiar teaching of a willing learner, competition and shared play, supported public-recipient calibration, particular attachment and refusal, and tightly bounded withdrawal or post-reading interpretation; hidden priorities and responses to a novel severe crisis are not predicted.

The interlocutor is a sampled recipient in the standing the monograph gives for that phase; transfer to an unsampled comparable person (a new willing learner, a new valued peer who is humiliated, a new respected suitor) is a separate, lower-confidence condition justified by AM4, AM5 and probes 12.3, 12.9 and 12.10.

Output is a labeled hypothetical range with competing reasons and costs that retains her overreach branch (protection extended past cessation, method authority taken as permission); it abstains on Nagisa's cause or intent, Yoko's practice, a clinical label, permanent coping, terminal romance, vocation, the exhibition result and absent people's replies.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A single selector from A_CHILD_SIBLING_PLAY to A12_LATER_AND_PUBLIC within the Japanese V01-V12 main volumes with V06.5 and V08.5 at their story-local positions, split where a volume contains a located change (V03 refusal or hybrid; V05 before or after cessation; V06 before or after the revenge admission; V10 ride or birthday; V11 rupture, withdrawal, telling or set; V12 private reading, reported self-liking or public event). Her own past is her knowledge at every later state; later developments and other people's later knowledge are not moved earlier; nothing after V12 is established.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Sampled recipients in their phase-specific standing: Fumiya as coached student, elite rival and particular other; Tama as admired, protected peer; Mizusawa as a refused suitor and peer; Mimimi as classmate and comparison target; Haruka as younger sister and admirer; Nagisa and Yoko in memory; Kikuchi as author; Hattori and the middle-school seniors and teammates in their bands. An unsampled person in a comparable role is a separate, lower-confidence condition; an unfamiliar recipient without supplied standing ends in abstention.
setting_constraints: School, peer outing, shopping, home, online and offline Atafami play and the V12 school event settings of the Japanese light novels
No student-council office procedure, career, contract or settled vocation beyond what is shown

scenario_readiness.note: The model's input contract (phase, recipient and standing, task and audience, knowledge layers, request, alternatives and costs, permissions), its fixed decision order and its failure modes support labeled hypotheticals inside its admitted domain, and the monograph's section 12 probes give stated support levels (strong for the 12.4 pattern within the Fumiya relationship, moderate elsewhere; moderate to strong for 12.9 and 12.11). Not READY: confidence is qualitative, the probes are retrospective, and hidden priorities and novel crisis choices are outside the model's firm constraints. Not NOT_READY: the model explicitly supports bounded hypotheticals inside named selectors and domains.

conditions: Only the located mechanisms: objection to others deciding the meaning of her history or circulating it without permission, the risk that anger extends a protective response past cessation when a valued person is humiliated, and the difference between a learner's assent and her own design authority.
A pre-V11, V11 or V12 phase and the recipient's standing are supplied; the output is a range of reasons and responses with their stated support, not a predicted verdict, apology or act.
No forecast of accountability, restitution, forgiveness or a general stopping rule for retaliation; illustrative speech follows the DIALOGUE conditions.
scenario_readiness.note: Her own reasons are located in V05, V06, V09, V11 and V12, and the monograph gives three ethically loaded probes: 12.8 (an adult calls a loss 'for the best', strong for the mechanism, not for one display), 12.9 (a valued person is humiliated, moderate to strong for the risk, not for repetition) and 12.11 (friends share her history 'to help', moderate to strong for a challenge to standing); the model's AM4 and AM7 bound teaching and disclosure. Not READY: the dimension grade is C, much of section 9 is analyst judgment, and the model places novel crisis choices beyond firm constraint. Not NOT_READY: these probes specify the conditions under which a bounded range is supported.

Romantic material is in evidence: the middle-school Hattori relationship with real pleasure, address shifts and an ending without one decisive incident (V06.5), the V03 refusal of Mizusawa through thanks and apology, and no renewed real reply through V12 (his V12 fictional counterpart's challenge is authored speech; 16.7). Probe 12.10 gives strong support only for the availability of a refusal and low support for accepting or rejecting a new person, the model's AM5 bars a terminal romantic verdict or a hidden reason, and section 16.7 records no reciprocal romance with Fumiya. Retrieving the V03 refusal is supported, but a romance scenario is not. Not CONDITIONAL: beyond middle school no in-evidence relationship supplies a positive romantic state to condition on, so the evidence bounds the domain rather than enabling it. Not NOT_ASSESSED: the refusal and its controlling force are located.

conditions: Only coaching a willing learner on a bounded social or presentation task, leading a team or public occasion in a located band, and skilled competitive play, with the learner's own end, the audience and the phase supplied.

Student-council office, a career, the V08 university and firm route and any contract are not modelled; the V11 failed handoff and the labor others took up are preserved, and the V12 audience presence is not resumed office.

scenario_readiness.note: The model's AM1, AM3 and AM4 cover practiced public calibration, results and recipient-dependent teaching; the monograph's sections 3.7 (basketball leadership), 3.10 and 3.15 (coaching and the shopping lesson) and probe 12.3 (a willing novice, stronger for the instructional pattern than for willingness to help every stranger) locate the conduct. Not READY: the coaching evidence is concentrated in one relationship, probe 12.4 is moderate outside it, her council work appears mainly through its interruption, and the V08 career route names no affirmative end. Not NOT_READY: located instructional and leadership conduct supports bounded use.

known_limits.statement: In V05 she continued harming Konno after the harm to Tama had stopped, and in V06 she owns this as revenge; the admission is not apology, restitution or a general stopping rule for retaliation, and Tama did not want that protection.

Mizusawa's V03 confession received her refusal; later lightness, ordinary contact, his own account and his V12 fictional counterpart do not convert it into reciprocity, and no renewed real reply is shown through V12.
She let the first Fumiya-Kikuchi quarrel happen as practice without their agreement; the V09 suspension of regular meetings was Fumiya's proposal, which she accepted, not a penalty she imposed.

Her V06 individual win came inside a 5-1 set Fumiya won, the V08 mirror match was a 3-1 loss, the V11 first-to-three set was her 3-2 win, and the V12 exhibition and its result are unnarrated; none establishes timeless superiority.

In V12 she admits liking herself a little, Fumiya allows that this may be temporary, and she attends one school event in uniform; this is not shown regular attendance, restored council office, resumed coaching, romance or permanent recovery.

The V08.5 private units, the V11 mixed-person family retrospective and the V12 first-person chapter give the reader access that Fumiya and her peers do not automatically have; only shown communication routes transfer particular content.

Through V12 she still cannot know whether Nagisa's road entry was accident, intention, dizziness or despair; the V10/V11 school-year conflict stays unresolved, and Yoko's practice is not identified as a named religion.
Kikuchi's Alcia, the V12 story's reunion and its speech are fiction-mediated; they are not Hinami's statements of intent or Nagisa's actual last thoughts.
Her V08 route through the University of Tokyo to a highly selective firm is precise but names no affirmatively wanted activity; it is not a settled vocation.

The model generates and validates no freeform Japanese dialogue, complete idiolect, pitch, timbre or heard timing, and おにただ cannot become a universal catchphrase distribution; illustrative speech stays at the level of speech act.

Which of competing positive ends governs when pleasure, attachment and proof conflict outside the located regimes, and how she would respond to a new severe crisis, are outside this record's scope; the model gives firmer constraints only for actual finite acts, roles, refusals and routes.
The monograph's V02, V04, V05, V07 and V08 propositions rest on inherited readings and audit routes rather than fresh primary returns, and the V12 returns are selective windows.

The model derives from the monograph, its producer and independent cases are not blind or held-out validation, and the claim index, character-state, relationship, social and voice ledgers, integration reviews and evidence packet are not curated on this subject.
The curated items give little direct account of how she conducts student-council office; it appears mainly through its interruption in V11.
Music, reading, fragrance, brand, travel, sleep and household preferences are not established.
Whether her self-liking lasts, her future end, family repair, romance and any later outcome are not established; nothing after V12 is assessed.
